title: CI demo-no-network guard does not ban real api-module calls from demo/ modules — only client.gleam is structurally checked
evidence: test.yml: `VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rn "api_helpers" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" || true)` / `RSVP_VERBS=$(grep -rnE "rsvp\\.(send|get|post|put|patch|delete)" ...)` — no ban on `import api/*`. demo_api.gleam:19: `import api/auth_api.{type AuthResponse, AuthResponse}`. lint_demo_network.py:113: `path = "client/src/client.gleam"` (only file scanned). Echo: `echo "Demo mode is fully client-side: no API/network imports in demo/, no unguarded api calls in client.gleam."`
detail: A demo/ arm calling e.g. application_api.bulk_reject_applications (the exact r1-blocker class) passes every lint: greps only catch api_helpers/rsvp-verbs/fetch, and the structural lint never reads demo/. The echoed invariant is already false in-tree.
recommended_fix: Add a grep banning `import api/` in client/src/demo/ (explicit allowlist for the type-only auth_api/api_error imports), or extend lint_demo_network.py to scan demo/ modules for api-module calls.

title: lint_demo_network.py's DEMO_INTERCEPTED manifest is prose-synced to demo_update.handle — the pillar-1 guard's load-bearing invariant is unverified
detail: The script never opens demo_update.gleam. If a refactor drops an intercept arm while the message stays listed, the lint passes and demo falls through to a real api call — the field notes' own lesson ('structural guard, not prose') applied to only half the mechanism. Manifest verified accurate today.
recommended_fix: Have the lint parse demo/demo_update.gleam and derive DEMO_INTERCEPTED from handled message arms (or assert each listed message has an arm there), failing on mismatch.

title: Fixture drift: client shows applicant 'Grace Kelly' while the downloaded PDF says 'Gráinne Foley' — the two-sources-of-truth diverged
detail: The r1 'real-person name' fix landed only server-side: the SPA renders Grace Kelly (famous name, rejection/eviction/CCJ story, email mismatched to the name), then the report PDF names her Gráinne Foley. The 'update BOTH sides' duplication failed on its first edit.
recommended_fix: Change the client fixture to first_name 'Gráinne', last_name 'Foley' (email already matches); consider deriving pdf_prebake payloads from one shared fixture source.

title: Six zero-caller exports shipped: decode_checked, all_fixture_jsons (+ private helpers), result_to_seed_error, capture_with_props, demo_api.check_session
evidence: `pub fn decode_checked(` / `pub fn all_fixture_jsons() -> List(#(String, String)) {` / `pub fn result_to_seed_error(result: Result(a, String)) -> Result(a, SeedError) {` / `pub fn capture_with_props(event: String, props: List(#(String, String))) -> Nil {` / `pub fn check_session(` — repo-wide grep for each name (excluding its definition) returns 0 hits; conformance test uses seed_* functions directly.
detail: R1 #28 class partially carries forward: the rework deleted the six refcheck wrappers but shipped new dead exports (all_fixture_jsons' only consumers are its own dead private helpers vacancies_json/applications_json).
recommended_fix: Delete the six unused functions and their private helpers; keep seed_* as the conformance suite's enumeration surface.

title: pdf_prebake: unused imports (compiler warnings) and still exits 0 when PDFs fail to bake
evidence:
Import block: `  type GetDocumentsByApplicationRow, type GetIncomeSourcesByApplicationRow,` and `import gleam/result` — zero `result.` or row-type usages in the body (grep: only the import lines). Failure branch ends main(): `    _ ->
      io.println(
        "FAILED: "` with no halt/non-zero exit anywhere in the module.
detail: R1 #20's exit-code half didn't land (only the env-override half did): a scripted regeneration cannot detect that PDFs failed, and every build emits unused-import warnings. AGENTS no-tech-debt rule.
recommended_fix: Remove the three unused imports; on failures > 0 call a nonzero exit (e.g. erlang halt(1) FFI or process.sleep-free `erlang` halt) so CI/scripts can detect failure.

title: download_timeout duplicated between demo_update.gleam and client.gleam (r1 #31 carry-forward, now only documented)
evidence: demo_update.gleam: `/// 90s download timeout — mirrors client.gleam's \`download_timeout\` so a` / `fn download_timeout(id: String) -> Effect(Msg) {` / `    global.set_timeout(90_000, fn() {` — client.gleam:6844: `fn download_timeout(analysis_id: String, delay_ms: Int) -> Effect(Msg) {`
detail: Two copies of the same timeout effect that can drift independently; the rework annotated the mirror instead of sharing one definition as r1 #31 recommended.
recommended_fix: Export client.gleam's parameterised download_timeout (or hoist to a demo/shared helper) and have demo_update call it with 90_000.
